T2 (REG-B46, R2, file A `recurring-invoices.schedule-outcome.spec.ts`): the plan's own G/W/T for T2 is "dom 31, from 2026-01-31 -> compute, then compute again from the result -> 2026-02-28 then 2026-03-31", and its "Fails today because" column says "first call returns 2026-01-31 (unchanged)". Verified via `npx jest src/recurring-invoices/recurring-invoices.schedule-outcome.spec.ts --verbose`: T2 is the only REG-token test that passes (all other 9 red tests — T1, T3, T5, T6, T7, T17, T18, T19, T31 — fail on their own named assertion, matching the plan's expected-failure table almost verbatim). I left T2 exactly as specified (it is a faithful, correct proof of R2 and will keep passing after the fix), but it is effectively behaving as a pin rather than a red test in the current unpatched code. Flagging for the lead/reviewer: either reclassify T2 as a pin (move outside `-t "REG-B"` scope) or accept that the red-gate command will show 9/10 (not 10/10) red tests in file A until this is reconciled — the DTO file's 4 REG/pin-adjacent T30 tests behaved exactly as the plan predicted (assertion failures via "resolved instead of rejected", no import/type errors).

T29 fails on its own `toBeDefined()` assertion (module genuinely absent, no stub needed since a dynamic `require`+try/catch pattern per the plan's §2.1 guidance avoids any import/build error). Pins T4, T8 (new describe blocks) and T20 (extended the existing "already claimed" test with the `recurringInvoice.update` assertion) all pass today, confirmed via `npx jest src/recurring-invoices/recurring-invoices.service.spec.ts --verbose` (12/12 green, including the 3 pre-existing describe blocks, unmodified in behavior). findings.detail: The form seeds nextRunAt once from `initial` (useState initializer, line 254) and handleSubmit unconditionally includes `nextRunAt: new Date(nextRunAt).toISOString()`; the API update() writes it whenever present. Scenario: operator opens /invoices/recurring/<id>/edit at 23:55 for a template due today (nextRunAt = today); at 00:00 the cron claims it (nextRunAt -> next month) and generates the invoice; at 00:03 the operator saves a notes change. The same happens if a colleague clicks Run Now on the list while the edit page is open. The spec accepts last-write-wins for scalar fields, but nextRunAt is the CAS-guarded cycle key, and re-opening it is precisely B46's symptom; dayOfWeek/dayOfMonth are already sent conditionally, nextRunAt is not.

One test does not fail today, contrary to the test-plan's own classification, and I did not alter or weaken it to force a false red — I judged that inventing an assertion outside the plan to manufacture failure would violate rule 7 (never make a test pass/fail by fabricating assertions on a mock I configured) more than reporting the discrepancy honestly.

T2 (REG-B46, R2, file A `recurring-invoices.schedule-outcome.spec.ts`): the plan's own G/W/T for T2 is "dom 31, from 2026-01-31 -> compute, then compute again from the result -> 2026-02-28 then 2026-03-31", and its "Fails today because" column says "first call returns 2026-01-31 (unchanged)". I traced the actual `calcNextRunAt` source (both by hand and by running it in a scratch Node script) and then confirmed with a real Jest run: for this specific input, the current buggy MONTHLY branch already returns 2026-02-28 then 2026-03-31 — the exact values the plan calls "correct" — because Jan 31's "+1 day" step always overflows into February regardless of `dom`, which accidentally produces the right month advance for this month-end fixture (the general T1-class bug — landing back in the same month when `dom` doesn't force an overflow — does not trigger here). Verified via `npx jest src/recurring-invoices/recurring-invoices.schedule-outcome.spec.ts --verbose`: T2 is the only REG-token test that passes (all other 9 red tests — T1, T3, T5, T6, T7, T17, T18, T19, T31 — fail on their own named assertion, matching the plan's expected-failure table almost verbatim). I left T2 exactly as specified (it is a faithful, correct proof of R2 and will keep passing after the fix), but it is effectively behaving as a pin rather than a red test in the current unpatched code. Flagging for the lead/reviewer: either reclassify T2 as a pin (move outside `-t "REG-B"` scope) or accept that the red-gate command will show 9/10 (not 10/10) red tests in file A until this is reconciled — the DTO file's 4 REG/pin-adjacent T30 tests behaved exactly as the plan predicted (assertion failures via "resolved instead of rejected", no import/type errors).

Everything else matches the package brief and test-plan exactly: T1, T3, T5, T6, T7 (MONTHLY schedule/claim), T17, T18, T19 (failure/success outcome), T31 (recurring item replace) all fail on their own concrete expected values (confirmed via a real Jest run, error messages match the plan's §6 table almost word-for-word — e.g. T1 "expected 7 received 6", T6 "toBeGreaterThan" fails on cycle 1, T18's exact array diff). T29 fails on its own `toBeDefined()` assertion (module genuinely absent, no stub needed since a dynamic `require`+try/catch pattern per the plan's §2.1 guidance avoids any import/build error). Pins T4, T8 (new describe blocks) and T20 (extended the existing "already claimed" test with the `recurringInvoice.update` assertion) all pass today, confirmed via `npx jest src/recurring-invoices/recurring-invoices.service.spec.ts --verbose` (12/12 green, including the 3 pre-existing describe blocks, unmodified in behavior). Applied the §2.2 rewrite of the "advances nextRunAt exactly once" pin (replaced the blanket `not.toHaveBeenCalled()` with the `nextRunWrites` filter) since it is in file B, in scope, and directly reconciles with my T18's SUCCESS-write expectation — without it this pin would start failing as soon as the implementation lands. Did not touch T21 or file D/C/E/G/H — out of package scope per the brief's explicit test-ID list.

confirmedFindings.summary: Package WP-API-OT is partial
confirmedFindings.detail:
Implementation is complete and byte-for-byte the plan's exact code for all three allowed files. However `npx jest src/order-templates --silent` shows 3 pre-existing failures I could not fix without touching a file outside my allowed set (order-templates.service.spec.ts is not in my file list):

describe("OrderTemplatesService — regulated license guard on reorder") at apps/api/src/order-templates/order-templates.service.spec.ts:19-108 (pre-existing, predates F13 — confirmed via `git log` showing it unchanged since commit 06828000 / F2-003, and TP-API-OT's prior append only added lines 292+). Its `ordersService` mock (line 24, 48) is `{ mergeAllPendingForCustomer: jest.fn()... }` only — it doesn't stub `loadActivePromotions`, `getCustomerPriceHistory`, or `resolveBuyerLinePrice`. My correct WP-API-OT implementation of `createOrderFromTemplate` now unconditionally calls `this.ordersService.loadActivePromotions(...)`, which is `undefined` on that mock, throwing `TypeError: this.ordersService.loadActivePromotions is not a function` in all 3 of that describe block's tests.

This is a real, verified regression against a pin test outside my scope, not a flaw in my implementation — every T9-T16/T23/T25/T26 test that governs WP-API-OT (in the new order-templates.pricing-and-items.spec.ts and update-order-template.dto.spec.ts) passes, and the file-list boundary explicitly forbids me from editing order-templates.service.spec.ts. The fix is a 3-line addition to that file's `ordersService` mock object at line 48: `loadActivePromotions: jest.fn().mockResolvedValue([]), getCustomerPriceHistory: jest.fn().mockResolvedValue({}), resolveBuyerLinePrice: jest.fn()` — flagging this for the orchestrator/reviewer to apply (or a later stage) since it's in a test file, not one of my three target files.

No other deviations — WP-ORDERS's two access-modifier changes (loadActivePromotions/resolveBuyerLinePrice made public) were already live on disk when I started (done by a prior/parallel package), so createOrderFromTemplate could call them directly; I did not touch orders.service.ts.

confirmedFindings.summary: The "accepts a full create-shaped body" fixture sends customerId "c1", which the DTO's inherited @IsUUID() rejects, so the spec fails.
confirmedFindings.detail: Ran `cd apps/api && npx jest src/recurring-invoices ...`: `UpdateRecurringInvoiceDto > T30 — accepts a full create-shaped body` fails with `Received promise rejected instead of resolved / BadRequestException`. `CreateRecurringInvoiceDto.customerId` carries `@IsUUID()` (create-recurring-invoice.dto.ts:29) and `PartialType` only adds `@IsOptional()`, so "c1" is a 400. confirmedFindings.summary: The new MONTHLY branch advances relative to `from` (= the stale stored nextRunAt), not relative to now, so an overdue template's claim still writes a past nextRunAt and the midnight cron re-selects it the next night — violating R4 / acceptance criterion 3.
confirmedFindings.detail: `calcNextRunAt` returns the earliest dayOfMonth occurrence strictly after `from`, and `generateInvoiceFromTemplate` passes `from = ri.nextRunAt`. The cron selects on `nextRunAt: { lte: new Date() }` (recurring-invoices.service.ts:302). B46 froze every MONTHLY template at its original due date (the old branch returned `dom` in the month of `from+1day`, i.e. `from` itself whenever dayOfMonth >= 2), so on the F13 deploy a template stuck at, say, 2025-03-20 advances only to 2025-04-20 — still <= now — and fires again the next night, and the next, minting one real invoice per night for ~18 nights until it catches up. Acceptance criterion 3 states "the claim's `data.nextRunAt` is strictly in the future"; spec R4 states the cron "cannot re-select a template it just ran". Neither holds for the exact population B46 damaged. T7 does not catch this: it only asserts the returned date is 2026-08-15, never that it is after `now`. The close-out plan (step 7) also only anticipates "the one extra deploy-night run per due MONTHLY template".
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Decide the catch-up rule explicitly and encode it: either advance from `max(from, today)` so the claim is always strictly future (one make-up invoice, then normal cadence), or keep per-cycle catch-up but make it an intentional, documented, tested behaviour with a bound. Whichever is chosen, add a test that asserts the claim's nextRunAt is > now for a template whose stored nextRunAt is months in the past.

confirmedFindings.summary: The two writes after invoicesService.create (the invoice link and the SUCCESS status) are outside the try/catch, so a throw there leaves a committed invoice behind a FAILED row whose UI hint invites a Run Now that mints a duplicate.
confirmedFindings.detail: Path: claim stamps `lastRunStatus FAILED` + `lastError "Generation was interrupted before the invoice was created"` and advances nextRunAt -> `invoicesService.create` succeeds and commits -> `prisma.invoice.update({ recurringInvoiceId })` (line 271-274) or the SUCCESS write (line 278-281) throws (connection loss, pool exhaustion). Neither is guarded, so the method throws with the provisional FAILED still on the row while a real invoice exists. The web card then renders "Generation was interrupted before the invoice was created — use Run Now to retry." (apps/web/app/(dashboard)/invoices/recurring/page.tsx:180-184), which is factually false. Clicking Run Now re-reads the row, and the CAS `where: { id, nextRunAt: ri.nextRunAt }` now matches the ADVANCED value, so the claim succeeds and a SECOND invoice is created for the same cycle — the exact duplicate the B9 claim exists to prevent. Spec decision D-A2 only checked that `invoicesService.create` has no post-commit step; it did not cover these two later writes.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Bring the link + SUCCESS writes under one named condition with the create, e.g. wrap them in a try/catch that records FAILED with the real message but explicitly does NOT restore nextRunAt (invoice exists), and give that state a distinct lastError text plus a card hint that does not tell the operator to re-run. Alternatively make the SUCCESS write best-effort (.catch(log)) so a post-commit hiccup never leaves a FAILED-with-invoice row.

confirmedFindings.summary: `parseFloat(x) || undefined` turns a 0 into undefined, so on the new edit page an operator can never clear a template's Invoice Discount or Shipping Fee back to 0.
confirmedFindings.detail: Lines 302-303 build the dto as `discount: parseFloat(discount) || undefined` / `shippingFee: parseFloat(shippingFee) || undefined`. A template with `discount: 25` edited to `0` sends no `discount` key; the service guard `...(dto.discount !== undefined && { discount: dto.discount })` (recurring-invoices.service.ts:129) therefore skips the column, the PATCH returns 200 and the "Recurring template updated" toast fires, and every future generated invoice keeps the old $25 discount. Same for shippingFee, and same for an emptied field (parseFloat("") === NaN -> undefined). Harmless in create mode (DB default 0), but the edit page is exactly the new surface WP-WEB-RECURRING adds, and this is a money field.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Send the parsed number whenever it is finite rather than truthy, e.g. `const d = parseFloat(discount); ... discount: Number.isFinite(d) ? d : undefined` (same for shippingFee), so 0 reaches the API.

confirmedFindings.summary: The post-Run-Now URL assertion matches the page the test is already on, so invoiceId is captured as "recurring", the guard can never fail, and the finally block never voids the generated invoice.
confirmedFindings.detail: After clicking Run Now the test asserts `toHaveURL(/\/invoices\/[^/]+$/)`. The current URL is `<base>/invoices/recurring`, which matches that regex, so the first poll passes immediately — before `router.push(/invoices/<id>)` can have run (the mutation is still in flight). `page.url().match(/\/invoices\/([^/?#]+)/)` then captures "recurring", so `expect(invoiceId, "Run Now did not navigate to an invoice URL").toBeTruthy()` can never fail, and the finally block POSTs `/api/v1/invoices/recurring/void`, which 404s and is swallowed. Every green run therefore leaves a real generated invoice on the shared e2e-routeflow tenant, contradicting the file's own header ("the Run Now invoice is voided there too"). It also makes the immediately following `page.goto("/invoices/recurring")` race the server's SUCCESS write, so the card can render the provisional "Failed" pill with no refetch to correct it within the 15s expect — a spurious red.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Assert on a URL shape that excludes the list page (e.g. `/\/invoices\/[0-9a-f-]{36}$/`) so the assertion actually waits for the navigation before capturing the id, and only then navigate back to the list.

confirmedFindings.summary: The cycle claim computes nextRunAt from ri.nextRunAt, so a backlogged MONTHLY template still gets a past nextRunAt and the cron re-fires it every night until the backlog clears — violating acceptance criterion 3 / R4 / spec §7.
confirmedFindings.detail: generateInvoiceFromTemplate calls `calcNextRunAt(..., ri.nextRunAt)` at :200, and calcNextRunAt (:28-53) returns the first dayOfMonth occurrence strictly after `from` — one month later, not "strictly in the future". Under B46 the old branch returned `from` unchanged (d.setDate(1) then `1 > dom` is false, then setDate(dom)), so every damaged MONTHLY template has nextRunAt FROZEN at its original due date, potentially many months back. The cron selects on `nextRunAt: { lte: new Date() }` (:302). I simulated the exact shipped MONTHLY branch: a template frozen at 2026-01-15 with today 2026-09-02 fires on 8 consecutive nights (Feb 15 → Sep 15) before it settles — 8 more customer invoices. Build-plan AC 3 ("the claim's data.nextRunAt is strictly in the future"), R4 ("the midnight cron's nextRunAt <= now filter cannot re-select a template it just ran") and spec §7 ("the nightly spam ends with one final run", echoed in close-out step 7 as "the one extra deploy-night run per due MONTHLY template") are all unmet for exactly the population B46 damaged. T7 does not catch it: its oracle only asserts month+1 from a fixed past `from`, so the requirement it claims (R4, "strictly-future") is not the property it exercises.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Decide the catch-up rule explicitly and encode it: either advance from `max(ri.nextRunAt, today)` (skip missed cycles, one invoice, matches AC3/§7), or keep month-by-month catch-up and correct R4/AC3/§7 plus add a test that pins the chosen behaviour for a `from` many months in the past. Whichever is chosen, add a regression test with `from` months before `now` asserting the claim's nextRunAt against `now`.

confirmedFindings.summary: `PATCH /order-templates/:id` with `items: null` passes validation and then throws a TypeError (500) instead of being rejected or treated as absent.
confirmedFindings.detail: I ran the shipped UpdateOrderTemplateDto through `new ValidationPipe({whitelist:true, transform:true, forbidNonWhitelisted:true})`: `{name:"x", items:null}` is ACCEPTED and comes back with `items === null` (class-validator's `@IsOptional()` skips all validators for null). update() then tests `dto.items === undefined` (:179), which is false, and reaches `items.map(...)` at :188 → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null` → 500. R20 requires malformed `items` to be a 400; the sibling implementation in recurring-invoices.service.ts:135 uses `if (!dto.items)` and is safe. No data is written (the throw precedes any write), so impact is a 500 rather than a 400.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Use `if (dto.items == null)` (or `!dto.items`) at order-templates.service.ts:179 so a null items key takes the scalar-only path, matching the recurring service; optionally add `@IsArray()`-level rejection by dropping `@IsOptional()` in favour of `@ValidateIf((_, v) => v !== undefined)`.

confirmedFindings.summary: The PATCH-items contract tests are tokened REG-B48 although they prove B09 (R20/R21), so B48's campaign proof set names tests that do not exercise B48.
confirmedFindings.detail: T23 (this file, line 18: "REG-B48 accepts items on a PATCH…") and T25/T26 (order-templates.pricing-and-items.spec.ts: "REG-B48 update() replaces items atomically…", "REG-B48 update() validates every item's product exists…") all exercise `update()`'s item-replacement path, which spec.md maps to R20/R21 = B09; the build plan's TP-API-OT explicitly says this package's proofs carry `REG-B48`/`REG-B09` tokens. scripts/campaign-check.mjs indexes proofs by the `REG-B###` token in the test's full name, so B48 (a T1 Critical whose ledger row flips to `proven` naming its REG tests) will be credited with three assertions that would still pass if the B48 pricing fix were reverted. The file's own docblock repeats the mislabel ("B48/R20"). B48 keeps five genuine proofs, so this is mis-attribution rather than a false green.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Rename the three titles (and the update-order-template.dto.spec.ts docblock) to `REG-B09 …`; the red gate filter `-t "REG-B"` still selects them.

confirmedFindings.summary: WP-ORDERS omitted the doc line the plan mandates on both newly-shared methods, and reported no deviation.

confirmedFindings.summary: The pre-existing "regulated license guard on reorder" suite mocks OrdersService with only `mergeAllPendingForCustomer`, so all three of its tests now die with a TypeError instead of exercising the guard.

confirmedFindings.summary: The "accepts a full create-shaped body" test uses `customerId: "c1"`, which fails `CreateRecurringInvoiceDto`'s `@IsUUID()`, so the test asserts a resolve and gets a 400.
confirmedFindings.detail: Verified by running `cd apps/api && npx jest src/recurring-invoices/dto`: 4 passed, 1 failed — `T30 — accepts a full create-shaped body` → "Received promise rejected instead of resolved. Rejected to value: [BadRequestException]". `UpdateRecurringInvoiceDto = PartialType(CreateRecurringInvoiceDto)` preserves the UUID validator (PartialType only adds @IsOptional), so "c1" is correctly rejected. The fixture only ever "passed" during the red phase because the DTO module did not exist and the ValidationPipe skipped an undefined metatype — a false pass, not evidence the fixture was valid. As written the test now reports the correct implementation as broken, and the plan's final jest command stays red.

confirmedFindings.summary: The post-"Run Now" URL assertion is tautological — the pre-click URL `/invoices/recurring` already matches `/\/invoices\/[^/]+$/` — so the guard proves nothing and the extracted `invoiceId` is usually the literal string "recurring".
confirmedFindings.detail: The test is on `/invoices/recurring` when it clicks Run Now, then asserts `await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/invoices\/[^/]+$/, { timeout: 20_000 })`. `https://host/invoices/recurring` satisfies that regex, so `toHaveURL` resolves on its first poll without waiting for any navigation. `page.url().match(/\/invoices\/([^/?#]+)/)` then captures "recurring", and `expect(invoiceId, "Run Now did not navigate to an invoice URL").toBeTruthy()` (line 311) passes vacuously. Consequences: (a) a regression where Run Now fails to navigate to the created invoice — the exact `router.push(`/invoices/${inv.id}`)` path in apps/web/app/(dashboard)/invoices/recurring/page.tsx:81 — is never caught; (b) the `finally` cleanup posts `/api/v1/invoices/recurring/void`, which is swallowed by `.catch(() => undefined)`, so every green run leaks a real generated invoice on the e2e seed tenant instead of voiding it.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Exclude the list route from the pattern and wait for a real navigation, e.g. `await expect(page).toHaveURL(/\/invoices\/(?!recurring$)[^/]+$/, { timeout: 20_000 })`, then extract with the same anchored pattern so `invoiceId` can never be "recurring".

confirmedFindings.summary: The new MONTHLY branch loops forever when a stored dayOfMonth is 0 or negative, hanging the Node event loop for the whole API process.
confirmedFindings.detail: `occurrence(y, m)` is `new Date(y, m, Math.min(dom, lastDay))`; for `dom <= 0` that lands in month m-1, so `next.getMonth() + 1` returns to month m and produces the identical date, and the `while (next.getTime() <= base.getTime())` at line 49 never advances. I confirmed this with a node simulation of the exact code in this session: dom=15 and dom=31 terminate in 1 iteration, while dom=0 and dom=-3 were still stuck at the same date after 1000 iterations. There is no `await` inside the loop, so a single such row blocks the event loop and the whole process — the midnight cron never reaches the remaining tenants and the API stops serving. Reachability: `RecurringInvoice.dayOfMonth` is a nullable Int with no DB constraint, and the very bug this change fixes (B92) is that `PATCH /recurring-invoices/:id` was completely unvalidated while its handler mapped `dayOfMonth` straight through (`...(dto.dayOfMonth !== undefined && { dayOfMonth: dto.dayOfMonth })`), so a production row can already hold 0 or a negative. The old code was total (it always returned) — this is a new hang, and the DTO's `@Min(1) @Max(28)` only protects rows written from now on.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Clamp the input before use, e.g. `const dom = Math.min(31, Math.max(1, Math.trunc(Number(dayOfMonth) || 1)))`, and/or bound the loop (a max of 2 iterations is sufficient for any valid dom) so a corrupt row degrades to a wrong-but-finite date instead of a hang.

confirmedFindings.summary: The provisional FAILED outcome is never narrowed once the invoice exists, so a failure in the link or SUCCESS write leaves a billed cycle labelled "interrupted before the invoice was created" — and the UI then tells the operator to Run Now, which duplicates the invoice.
confirmedFindings.detail: The try/catch covers only `invoicesService.create` (lines 218-255). Everything after it runs unguarded: the autoSend email (its own catch), then `invoice.update({ data: { recurringInvoiceId } })` at line 271, then the SUCCESS write at line 278-281. If either uncaught write throws — or the process is SIGTERM'd mid-cron, which happens on any Railway deploy that overlaps the midnight run — the row keeps `lastRunStatus: "FAILED"` and `lastError: "Generation was interrupted before the invoice was created"` even though the invoice WAS created and, with autoSend on, already emailed to the customer. nextRunAt stays advanced (correctly, since the invoice exists), so the operator reading the new card sees the red pill and the danger line `{lastError} — use Run Now to retry.` (apps/web/app/(dashboard)/invoices/recurring/page.tsx:180-184), and Run Now unconditionally claims the current nextRunAt and mints a SECOND invoice for the same cycle — a duplicate bill and a duplicate customer email. The provisional-FAILED design is sound for the pre-create window; the gap is that nothing narrows it once `create` has returned.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Immediately after `create` returns (before the autoSend/link block) rewrite lastError to a state that distinguishes "invoice created, bookkeeping incomplete" from "nothing was created" — e.g. a distinct message, or wrap lines 259-281 in a try/catch that records that state and logs, rather than letting the throw escape. Whatever the wording, the web/mobile FAILED copy must not tell the operator to retry a cycle that already billed.

confirmedFindings.summary: On the new edit page a cleared or zeroed field is silently dropped from the PATCH, so a template's invoice discount and shipping fee can never be set back to 0 and its notes/terms can never be cleared — while the UI reports success.
confirmedFindings.detail: handleSubmit builds the dto with `notes: notes.trim() || undefined` (300), `terms: terms.trim() || undefined` (301), `discount: parseFloat(discount) || undefined` (302), `shippingFee: parseFloat(shippingFee) || undefined` (303). `0` and `""` are falsy, so those keys become undefined; axios JSON.stringify drops undefined keys; and `RecurringInvoicesService.update` only writes a field when it is `!== undefined` (`...(dto.discount !== undefined && { discount: dto.discount })`). Concretely: a template with discount 25.00, the operator clears the Invoice Discount field (or types 0) and saves — the toast reads "Recurring template updated", the page returns to the list, and the next generated invoice still deducts 25.00. Same for Shipping Fee, and for clearing Notes or Payment Terms. This pattern was harmless in the create-only page it was extracted from (the API defaults these to 0/null on create); it becomes silent data loss the moment the same dto shape is reused for PATCH, which is what WP-WEB-RECURRING did.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: In edit mode send the parsed values unconditionally: `discount: Number.isFinite(parseFloat(discount)) ? parseFloat(discount) : 0`, same for shippingFee, and `notes: notes.trim()` / `terms: terms.trim()` (empty string clears them) — or branch the dto construction on `mode`, keeping the `|| undefined` shape only for create.

confirmedFindings.summary: The "Run Now navigated to the new invoice" guard also matches the list URL it started on, so it can pass without navigating and then leak a real invoice past the cleanup.

Any invoice that was in fact generated is then left on the e2e-routeflow seed tenant with no cleanup, and the assertion that was supposed to prove navigation proves nothing.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Anchor the regex on the id shape rather than "anything after /invoices/", e.g. `/\/invoices\/(?!recurring$)[0-9a-f-]{36}$/`, so staying on the list page fails the assertion instead of passing it.

confirmedFindings.summary: A failure after invoicesService.create succeeds leaves the template stamped FAILED with "interrupted before the invoice was created" while the invoice exists and nextRunAt is already advanced, and the UI's "use Run Now to retry" then mints a duplicate invoice and skips the next cycle.
confirmedFindings.detail: generateInvoiceFromTemplate only rolls back inside the `catch` around `invoicesService.create` (lines 214-254). The two writes after it — `invoice.update({ data: { recurringInvoiceId } })` at line 271-274 and the SUCCESS stamp at line 278-281 — are outside any try/catch. If either throws (transient DB error, connection reset, container restart mid-cycle), the invoice HAS been created and committed, nextRunAt is already advanced by the claim, and the row keeps the claim's provisional `lastRunStatus: "FAILED"` / `lastError: "Generation was interrupted before the invoice was created"`. The operator's list card (apps/web/app/(dashboard)/invoices/recurring/page.tsx:180-185) then renders exactly that message plus "— use Run Now to retry". Clicking Run Now re-reads the row, the claim `where: { id, nextRunAt: ri.nextRunAt }` matches the already-advanced value, so a SECOND invoice is created for the same period AND nextRunAt advances a second time, silently skipping the following cycle. Net for a MONTHLY template: the customer gets two invoices for one month and none for the next, with logs that say the run failed.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Decide the post-create failure contract and make the state honest: either wrap the link + SUCCESS writes in their own try/catch that records a distinct lastError (e.g. "invoice <id> was created but the run could not be finalized") without inviting a retry, or write SUCCESS first and link second. Whatever is chosen, the card's "use Run Now to retry" copy must only appear for the give-the-cycle-back (create-threw) case, since only that case restored nextRunAt.

confirmedFindings.summary: The rewritten MONTHLY branch advances strictly past `from`, not past today, so a template whose nextRunAt lags generates one invoice per night until it catches up — and the new edit page lets an operator set a past Next Run Date.

I ran the exact algorithm from lines 34-53 with dom=15 and from=2026-01-15 against today's date: it returns 2026-02-15, still in the past; the following seven nightly cron passes return 2026-03-15 … 2026-09-15, i.e. seven real invoices to the customer on seven consecutive nights before the schedule reaches the future. This directly contradicts the plan's acceptance criterion 3 ("the claim's data.nextRunAt is strictly in the future") — T7 in recurring-invoices.schedule-outcome.spec.ts:119 only proves the claim advances one month past ri.nextRunAt, never that it lands in the future. Reachable today: deactivate() and activate() (lines 165-178) never touch nextRunAt, so pausing a MONTHLY template for N months and resuming it fires N nightly invoices; POST /recurring-invoices accepts any @IsDateString nextRunAt including a past one; and F13 newly ships an edit page whose Next Run Date field (RecurringInvoiceForm.tsx, `<input type="date">` with no `min`) lets an operator set a past date and save it through the now-validated PATCH.
confirmedFindings.fixHint: Decide the catch-up policy explicitly for MONTHLY (and consider WEEKLY/BIWEEKLY, which have the same property): either clamp the claim so the written nextRunAt is strictly greater than `new Date()` (skip missed cycles, one invoice on catch-up), or keep per-cycle catch-up but bound it. Add a test that asserts the claimed nextRunAt is in the future for a `from` months in the past.

confirmedFindings.summary: On the new edit page, clearing Notes, Payment Terms, Invoice Discount or Shipping Fee is silently discarded — the fields are sent as undefined, the PATCH omits them, and the operator gets a success toast.

Scenario: operator opens /invoices/recurring/<id>/edit at 23:55 for a template due today (nextRunAt = today); at 00:00 the cron claims it (nextRunAt -> next month) and generates the invoice; at 00:03 the operator saves a notes change. The PATCH carries nextRunAt = today -> the template is due again -> the next midnight generates a second invoice for the same cycle (advanceFrom = now, so it does not loop, but the duplicate is minted). The same happens if a colleague clicks Run Now on the list while the edit page is open. The spec accepts last-write-wins for scalar fields, but nextRunAt is the CAS-guarded cycle key, and re-opening it is precisely B46's symptom; dayOfWeek/dayOfMonth are already sent conditionally, nextRunAt is not.
